gaps.sentence: To such an extent ___ prices risen that buyers withdrew.
gaps.hint: To such an extent + past perfect
gaps.explanation: To such an extent had prices risen that… — emphatic result.

gaps.sentence: So loud ___ the music that the neighbours called the police.
gaps.explanation: 'So loud was the music that …' — fronted 'so + adj' with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Also worth ___ is the museum's medieval wing.
gaps.explanation: Also worth noting is… — fronted comment structure.

gaps.sentence: At no time ___ the crew aware of the danger.
gaps.explanation: 'At no time was the crew aware' — inverted past simple of be.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ she apologise, she also paid for the damage.
gaps.explanation: Not only did she…, (but) she also… — inversion after not only.

gaps.sentence: ___ it not been for your help, we would have failed.
gaps.explanation: Had it not been for = if it hadn't been for — fixed inverted conditional.

gaps.sentence: So rapid ___ the spread of the fire that the building was lost.
gaps.explanation: 'So rapid was the spread that …' — fronted 'so + adj' with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Little did the suspects ___ that the police were listening.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did they know' — 'know' as bare verb after the inverted auxiliary 'did'.
